In this petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner has challenged the Order, dated 06.02.2026 (Annexure-I), passed by the State Information Commissioner, APIC, in Case No. APIC-764/2025, in so far as it directs the petitioner to furnish information pertaining to serial Nos. 4, 5, 8 & 9 of the RTI Application dated 27.06.2025; and the Show Cause Notice, dated 06.03.2026, (ANNEXURE-2) issued to the petitioner under Section 20(1) of the Right to Information Act, 2005; and also prayed for quashing Case No. APIC- 764/2025; and for declaration that information relating to land acquisition for the Frontier Highway Project (NH-913), being a defence-strategic infrastructure project acquired under Section 40(1) and (4) of the RFCTLARR Act,
2013, is exempted from disclosure under Section 8(1)(a) of the Right to Information Act, 2005.

3. Mr. Sonar, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is the PIO-cum-District Land Revenue and Settlement Officer (DLRSO), Palin, in Kra Daadi District and vide impugned order, dated 06.02.2026, the State Information Commissioner, APIC, in Case No. APIC-764/2025,
has directed him to disclose information at serial Nos. 4, 5, 8 & 9 of the RTI Application, dated 27.06.2025; and also issued the Show Cause Notice, dated 06.03.2026, calling upon the petitioner to show cause on 01.04.2026, as to why penalty of Rs. 25,000/- should not be imposed, under Section 20(1) of the RTI Act, 2005.

3.1 Mr. Sonar, further submits that the information, which was directed to be provided by the State Information Commissioner, relates to land acquisition for a defence-strategic highway project,
specifically the Frontier Highway (NH-913), of Huri-Taliha stretch; when such disclosure is prohibited by a binding Government Circular and exempted under Section 8(1)(a) (national security) and Section 8(1)(j) (third-party privacy) of the RTI Act; and the petitioner Page No.# 3/5 herein had withheld the information at serial Nos. 4, 5, 8 & 9 of the RTI Application, dated 27.06.2025; comprising of bank account details and compensation particulars of individual land-affected beneficiaries, on the ground that the Frontier Highway is a defence-strategic project acquired under Section 40(1) of the Act of 2013; and that the acquisition affects the sovereignty and integrity of India, covered by the national security exemption, under Section 8(1)(a) RTI Act and by Circular No. Secy(LM)-06/2021, dated 15.03.2021, and that the financial data of beneficiaries is protected under Section 8(1)(j).
3.2

It is the further submission of Mr. Sonar that the State Information Commissioner, APIC, vide impugned order, dated 06.02.2026, has also directed the petitioner to disclose the withheld information, ignoring the national security exemption and also issued Show Cause Notice, dated 06.03.2026, threatening penalty of Rs. 25,000/- under Section 20(1) RTI Act.

3.3 Mr. Sonar has also pointed out that the respondent No. 2 has preferred the second appeal without exhausting the procedure of filing of the first appeal and referring to a decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Chief Information Commissioner And Another Vs. State of Manipur And Another, reported in (2011) 15 SCC, page No. 1; and also, a decision of the High Court of Delhi, in the case of Ved Prakash Aggarwal Vs. Deputy Registrar (CR-1), Central Information Commission, reported in MANU/DE/0800/2020; Mr. Sonar submits that without filing the first appeal, the respondent No. 2 cannot directly file a second appeal, in view of Section 19(3) of the Right to Information Act, and Rule 10(2) & (3) of the Right to Information Rules, 2010; and since,

show-cause notice was issued to him, Page No.# 4/5 threatening to impose penalty of Rs. 25,000/-;
the said order and also, the notice suffers from the vice of illegality and procedural irregularity, and the same requires interference of this Court and therefore, Mr. Sonar has contended to consider the prayer made in this writ petition, and to stay the impugned notice and the order.
4.

Mr. Saikia, learned counsel for the respondent No. 1 also submits that the respondent No. 2 herein has preferred the second appeal, without preferring the first appeal before the concerned appellate authority.
5. The submission of the learned counsel for both the parties needs further consideration.
6. At this stage, notice be issued to the respondents, returnable in 4 (four) weeks.
7. However, no formal notice is required to be issued to the respondent No. 1, since Mr. R. Saikia has entered appearance for the respondent No. 1 and received notice.
But, extra requisite copy of the petition be furnished to him during the course of the day.

8. Steps upon respondent No. 2 be taken by speed post and also by usual process, within a week from today.
9.
List the matter after 4 (four) weeks.

10. Also, taking note of the submission of Mr. R. Sonar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. R.
Saikia, learned counsel for the respondent No. 1; and further, taking note of the fact that the second appeal was filed without preferring the first appeal, a prima-facie case appears to be made out in favour of the petitioner and accordingly, the impugned order, dated 06.02.2026 and the Page No.#
5/5 Show Cause Notice, dated 06.03.2026; stands stayed, till the returnable date.
